Stepwise Selection of the Covariates of a Small Area Model

Source: R/step_sae.R
step_sae.Rd

Selects the covariates of a fitted fastsae model by stepwise search (backward, forward or both) on an information criterion, refitting the model with the same settings (family, spatial or temporal structure, engine, ...) at every step.

Usage

step_sae(
  object,
  scope = NULL,
  direction = c("both", "backward", "forward"),
  criterion = NULL,
  steps = 1000,
  trace = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model: eblup_fh(), eblup_sfh(), eblup_stfh(), eblup_bhf(), eblup_twofold(), hb_area(), hb_unit() or hb_twofold().

scope

The range of models searched: a formula with the largest set of covariates (the upper model), or a list with formulas lower and upper. Default: the covariates of object as upper model and the intercept-only model as lower model. Forward selection needs an upper model larger than object.

direction

"both" (default), "backward" or "forward".

criterion

Information criterion to minimise. EBLUP models: "AIC", "BIC" (default) or "KIC". HB models: "LCPO" (default with inla_engine()), "WAIC" (default with jax_engine()) or "DIC".

steps

Maximum number of steps. Default 1000.

trace

Logical; print the criterion of each candidate model. Default TRUE.

Value

An object of class "fastsae_step": a list with model (the selected model, fitted with the settings of object), path (a data frame with the term added or dropped at each step and the criterion), criterion, direction, and the initial and final formulas.

Details

EBLUP models. The criteria are computed from the full Gaussian log-likelihood \(\ell\) at the estimates, with \(k\) the number of coefficients plus variance parameters: \(\mathrm{AIC} = -2\ell + 2k\), \(\mathrm{BIC} = -2\ell + k \log m\) and \(\mathrm{KIC} = -2\ell + 3k\) (Marhuenda, Morales and Pardo 2014; the analytic criteria of emdi::step()). The restricted (REML) likelihood depends on the covariates through \(X\) and cannot compare models with different covariates, so models with a method argument are fitted by ML during the search; the selected model is then refitted with the method of object. eblup_stfh() has no ML fit and is compared through the likelihood at its REML estimates. Only sampled domains enter the criteria.

HB models (every family). "LCPO", the negative mean log conditional predictive ordinate \(-\frac{1}{m}\sum_d \log \mathrm{CPO}_d\) (leave-one-out cross-validation; Held, Schrödle and Rue 2010), and "WAIC" (Watanabe 2010) estimate the out-of-sample predictive accuracy; "DIC" (Spiegelhalter et al. 2002) is less reliable for hierarchical models. With one observation per area and an area random effect, WAIC is unstable (Vehtari, Gelman and Gabry 2017): in a simulation of a binomial area-level model (40 areas, two true and two noise covariates) WAIC selected exactly the true covariates in 27% of the replicates and dropped a true one in 13%, LCPO in 70% (benchmarks/validation/step_sae.R). LCPO is therefore the default with inla_engine(); jax_engine() has no CPO and uses WAIC. With jax_engine() every candidate model is an MCMC fit, so the search can take long; the criteria then also carry Monte Carlo error.

Spatial and temporal models. Every candidate is fitted with the spatial or temporal structure of object. Selecting the covariates without the spatial effect and adding it afterwards is not equivalent: a spatially smooth covariate and the spatial random effect explain the same variation (spatial confounding), so a covariate kept by a non-spatial model may be redundant, and its coefficient can change markedly, once the spatial effect is in the model (Reich, Hodges and Zadnik 2006; Hodges and Reich 2010). In the simulation above, with a spatial area effect and a spatially smooth noise covariate, the Fay-Herriot model kept that covariate in 20% of the replicates and the spatial Fay-Herriot model in 8%. Check the residual spatial autocorrelation of the selected model, e.g. with spatial_test().

The model is refitted by evaluating its call with a new formula in the environment where step_sae() is called, so the data and other arguments of the call must be available there.

References

Held, L., Schrödle, B. and Rue, H. (2010). Posterior and cross-validatory predictive checks: a comparison of MCMC and INLA. In T. Kneib and G. Tutz (eds.), Statistical Modelling and Regression Structures, 91-110. Physica-Verlag.

Hodges, J. S. and Reich, B. J. (2010). Adding spatially-correlated errors can mess up the fixed effect you love. The American Statistician, 64(4), 325-334.

Marhuenda, Y., Morales, D. and Pardo, M. C. (2014). Information criteria for Fay-Herriot model selection. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 70, 268-280.

Reich, B. J., Hodges, J. S. and Zadnik, V. (2006). Effects of residual smoothing on the posterior of the fixed effects in disease-mapping models. Biometrics, 62(4), 1197-1206.

Spiegelhalter, D. J., Best, N. G., Carlin, B. P. and van der Linde, A. (2002). Bayesian measures of model complexity and fit. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 64(4), 583-639.

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27(5), 1413-1432.

Watanabe, S. (2010). Asymptotic equivalence of Bayes cross validation and widely applicable information criterion in singular learning theory. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 11, 3571-3594.

See also

compare_sae, spatial_test

Examples

data(mys)
fit <- eblup_fh(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, vardir = "vardir", data = mys, print_result = FALSE)
sel <- step_sae(fit, criterion = "BIC")
#> Start: BIC = 147.3513 (y ~ x1 + x2 + x3)
#>    Step      BIC
#>    - x1 143.9140
#>    - x3 144.2980
#>    - x2 144.7444
#>  <none> 147.3513
#> Step: - x1: BIC = 143.914
#>    Step      BIC
#>    - x3 141.0402
#>    - x2 141.6679
#>  <none> 143.9140
#>    + x1 147.3513
#> Step: - x3: BIC = 141.0402
#>    Step      BIC
#>  <none> 141.0402
#>    + x3 143.9140
#>    + x1 144.2980
#>    - x2 149.7081
sel
#> 
#> ── Stepwise covariate selection (BIC, both) ────────────────────────────────────
#> Initial model: y ~ x1 + x2 + x3
#> Final model: y ~ x2
#> 
#>  Step      BIC
#>       147.3513
#>  - x1 143.9140
#>  - x3 141.0402
sel$model$formula
#> y ~ x2
#> <environment: 0x55caf6be7758>
